name: Comparatives & Superlatives
moduleIntroduction: Welcome to the Comparatives & Superlatives module! This is how we compare things in English. In French, you almost always use 'Plus' (*plus grand, plus intelligent*). In English, we have two systems: adding a tail (-er) or using a helper (more). If you use the French logic for everything, you will make mistakes like 'more big' or 'the most small'.
contrastiveExplanation:
Short Adjectives (1 syllable):
English: Add -er (Bigger) or -est (Biggest).
French: Uses 'Plus' (Plus grand).

Long Adjectives (2+ syllables):
English: Use 'More' (More expensive) or 'The Most' (The most expensive).
French: Uses 'Plus' (Plus cher).

Connecting Words:
English: Better THAN me.
French: Meilleur QUE moi. (Beware: 'Que' usually means 'That', but here it means 'Than').

commonErrors.frenchConnection: Applying French logic ('plus' = 'more') to short words.
Applying French logic ('le plus' = 'the most') to short words.
Using both systems at once for emphasis.

items.questionText: My brother is ___ than me.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Tall' is a short word (1 syllable), so we add '-er'.

items.questionText: Douala is ___ than Buea.
This is the ___ car in the shop.
Your fufu is ___ than mine.
Today is ___ than yesterday.
The weather is ___ today.
He is the ___ boy in class.
A plane is ___ than a car.
She is ___ than her sister.
This bag is ___ than that one.
items.feedback: Correct! Adjectives ending in 'y' change to 'ier'.

items.questionText: Who is the ___ person you know?
My room is ___ than yours.
July is the ___ month.
This exercise is ___.
items.feedback: Correct! This is a simple sentence, no comparison yet.

items.questionText: But the next one is ___.
items.feedback: Correct! Comparing to the first one -> Harder.

items.questionText: Mount Cameroon is ___.
It is the ___ mountain in West Africa.
This knife is ___ than that one.
He is ___ than his father.
I am the ___ in my family.
This phone is ___ than my old one.
She is the ___ girl in school.
items.feedback: Correct! Long adjective superlative -> The most beautiful.

items.questionText: English is ___ than French.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Easy' ends in 'y', so it becomes 'easier', even though it has 2 syllables.

items.questionText: The book is interesting, but the movie is ___.
He is taller ___ me.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Than' is for comparison. 'That' is for pointing.

items.questionText: My car is as fast ___ yours.
This road is ___ dangerous than the other one.
He is the ___ player on the team.
This is the ___ day of my life.
It is ___ comfortable here.
She is not as tall ___ her mother.
Which subject is ___?
items.feedback: Correct! Asking for the superlative among all subjects.

items.questionText: I am ___ than I was yesterday.
This problem is ___ than the last one.
He is famous, but she is ___.
My bag is the same ___ yours.
He drives ___ than his brother.
It is getting ___.
items.feedback: Correct! Repeated comparative for changing situations.

items.questionText: Of the two sisters, Ngono is the ___.
items.feedback: Correct! When comparing only TWO, we use the comparative form (the older), even with 'the'.

items.questionText: That is the ___ joke I ever heard.
The more you study, ___ you learn.
items.feedback: Correct! Double comparative structure: 'The X..., the Y...'.

items.questionText: This car is ___ better than the old one.
items.feedback: Correct! Use 'much' (or 'far') to emphasize a comparative. Never use 'more better'.

items.questionText: She is my ___ sister.
items.feedback: Correct! Within a family, 'elder' is often used before the noun.

items.questionText: The situation went from bad to ___.
This is ___ expensive hotel in the city.
items.feedback: Correct! 'The least' is the superlative of 'less'.

items.questionText: He is ___ to me.
items.feedback: Correct! Latin comparatives (superior, inferior, senior) do not take -er or more.

items.questionText: This is by far ___ cake I have tasted.
items.feedback: Correct! 'By far' is used to emphasize superlatives.

items.questionText: The faster you run, ___ tired you get.
items.feedback: Correct! Double comparative: 'The faster..., the more...'

items.questionText: She looks ___ older than her age.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Slightly' is a modifier for comparatives.

items.questionText: He is one of the ___ men in the world.
items.feedback: Correct! 'One of the' + Superlative + Plural Noun.

items.questionText: Can you go any ___?
items.feedback: Correct! 'Further' means 'more' (abstract). 'Farther' is physical distance (though often interchangeable). In this context (continue), 'further' is better.

items.questionText: It is not ___ warm as yesterday.
items.feedback: Correct! In negative comparisons, we can use 'not SO... as' instead of 'not AS... as'.

items.questionText: She is the ___ of the three girls.
I prefer coffee ___ tea.
items.feedback: Correct! We say 'Prefer X to Y', not 'than'.

items.questionText: That is the ___ idea I have ever heard.
items.feedback: Correct! Superlative + Present Perfect (have ever heard).

items.questionText: He is ___ intelligent than his brother.
This dress is twice as ___ as that one.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Twice as... as' uses the base adjective.

items.questionText: He is the ___ runner on the team.
My computer is ___ to yours.
The ___ you wait, the harder it becomes.
items.feedback: Correct! Double comparative 'The longer..., the harder...'.
